questions.prompt: Walk through how Relay keeps the local-destination import correct when a worker crashes, from upload to the last committed batch.

keyPoints.text: The upload is hashed while it is written, so the stored file and the recorded file_hash are the same bytes, and every worker rehashes the file and refuses on mismatch.
keyPoints.quote: every time a worker opens the file it rehashes

keyPoints.text: Parsing resumes by logical record count, not byte offset, because quoted values can contain newlines.
keyPoints.quote: the durable position is a logical record count

keyPoints.text: Staged rows and parse_checkpoint commit in one transaction, and replayed batches are harmless because import_rows inserts ignore conflicts.
keyPoints.quote: so a replayed batch is harmless

keyPoints.text: PostgreSQL, not worker memory, owns progress: a cached cursor that disagrees with the database checkpoint is dropped.
keyPoints.quote: PostgreSQL, not worker memory, owns progress.

keyPoints.text: Contact inserts and the commit checkpoint advance in the same transaction, so the crash windows before and after commit are symmetric.
The destination's unique (org_id,email) constraint is the final arbiter, so rerunning a batch cannot create a duplicate and existing data is never overwritten.
keyPoints.quote: Destination uniqueness is the final arbiter

questions.prompt: Explain how Relay guarantees that only the exact version a reviewer approved is imported.

keyPoints.text: Saving a mapping or correcting a row bumps mapping_version, resets validation and clears approved_hash in the same UPDATE.
There is no path that changes what will be imported while an approval stays attached.
keyPoints.quote: There is no path that changes

keyPoints.text: The approval hash covers the file hash, mapping version, schema version, schema hash and destination.
The hash is a version binding, not a signature; reviewer permission is checked separately.
keyPoints.quote: it is a version binding, not a signature

keyPoints.text: Approving requires review status and the exact version the reviewer saw; a stale approval gets 409.
The C# worker rebuilds the identical hash, and nothing but the end-to-end suites checks the two implementations agree.
The worker re-verifies the approval inside every batch transaction after locking the job, so a racing mapping edit cannot slip between check and effect.
keyPoints.quote: A mapping edit racing the import cannot slip

questions.prompt: Why does the external test-api destination need an outbox, uncertainty states and receipt lookup, and where does that guarantee stop?

keyPoints.text: The external destination has its own transactions, so no shared transaction can hold both its effects and Relay's checkpoint.
Rows are copied into the delivery outbox with a stable job, version and row key, committed before any network I/O.
The worker asks the destination for receipts before sending, which recovers the commit/response-loss window after a restart.
keyPoints.quote: Receipt lookup also recovers the commit/response-loss window

keyPoints.text: Missing keys are marked uncertain before the POST, so a crash mid-flight leaves a record that the rows may have been sent.
keyPoints.quote: the database already says "I may have sent this."

keyPoints.text: The destination returns the original outcome for a replayed key and rejects a replayed key with a changed payload.
keyPoints.quote: so the key cannot be silently reused

keyPoints.text: The guarantee depends on the test API's contract; against a destination without unique keyed receipts it degrades to at-least-once.
keyPoints.quote: this entire mechanism degrades to at-least-once
